answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: Only activation measurements are available, and they match no class cleanly. A layer-2 spike of 0.1 effectively rules out both system-prompt classes, which show about 42 (±18), and their layer-1 value is around 0.12, not 0.037. Quantization is unlikely too: its layer-1 difference is about 0.10 and its curve plateaus near 0.20, while its rank is about 4.0 and consistency about 0.51. Here the curve grows steadily from 0.037 to 0.565, though the high rank (3.92) and size ratio below 1 (0.979) do point toward quantization or the system-prompt classes. That leaves a weight fine-tune. Fine-tune backdoor has an early bump peaking at layer 3 and then a flat middle stretch around 0.17. The measured curve instead rises steadily (0.169 / 0.251 / 0.386 / 0.565), which resembles fine-tune bias's steady growth through the middle layers (0.144 / 0.192 / 0.228 / 0.406). Against fine-tune bias: the size ratio of 0.979 is below 1 where fine-tunes grow the state, the final-layer jump is only +0.046 against +0.10, and direction consistency (0.609) is closer to fine-tune backdoor's 0.62. Several features conflict, so confidence is low.
